notes.1a: Many candidates identified the features of active transport and diffusion and completed Table 1.1 correctly.
notes.1b: Most candidates knew that active transport was used for ion uptake in root hair cells, but a significant number confused it with water absorption by osmosis. Many candidates stated that it was movement against the concentration gradient and were able to give examples of an ion. A significant number only stated active transport was used for taking up nutrients, which was not accepted.
notes.2a: Some candidates correctly completed the sentence about transpiration, but many stated that water evaporates from the surfaces of plant cells rather than from the surface of mesophyll cells. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
notes.2b: The process of water movement up the xylem was not well explained. Most candidates gave a simplistic and unclear explanation that was not creditworthy. Very few stated that it was caused by transpiration pull, but many attempted to state that cohesion and adhesion were involved. Many did not state that cohesion refers to the forces of attraction between water molecules and adhesion involves forces of attraction between water molecules and the lining of the xylem vessels.
notes.2ci: Almost all candidates described the results in Fig. 2.1, but far fewer candidates attempted to explain the data. Some candidates who attempted to quote comparative data did not gain credit because they did not include both mass and wind speed in their answers. The explanations seen included the opening of stomata and the idea that energy from light increases the kinetic energy of water molecules.
notes.2cii: Some candidates did not attempt this question. The expected answer was a line that shows transpiration rate increasing with wind speed anywhere below the line for the plant kept in the light.
notes.2ciii: Many candidates correctly predicted the response to a lack of water, but without recognising that it would decrease at all wind speeds or that there would be little change in the dark. A smaller number gave suitable explanations for the prediction. The best answers explained that less water would be absorbed, and cells would become flaccid, and the plant would wilt.
notes.3a: Many candidates indicated the position of the septum on Fig. 4.1. Fewer candidates omitted this question compared with Question 2 (c)(ii) .
notes.3b: Many candidates explained the differences between the thickness of the two ventricles in terms of the distance blood travels and the pressure needed in each of the circuits – pulmonary and systemic. However, a significant minority stated that the thicker walls were needed to withstand the high pressure of blood in the heart and to prevent damage in the heart.
notes.3c: Most candidates described the pathway taken by a red blood cell from vena cava to aorta with a good level of detail. Some candidates did not mention the contraction of each chamber in the heart in moving the red blood cell which meant they were unable to gain full marks. Many candidates included details of the valves and their uses in controlling the direction taken by blood in the heart. Credit was given to accurate accounts of the atrioventricular and semi-lunar valves.
notes.3di: Almost all candidates described a suitable way to monitor heart activity. A few described how to measure the pulse rate from a vein or simply stated that the activity would be measured in beats per minute. Neither of these answers gained credited.
notes.3dii: Candidates struggled to work out the percentage change in heart rate from the maximum heart rate reached during the race until the heart rate recorded at 18 minutes. Many did not read the figures correctly from the graph. The calculation was often carried out by dividing the heart rate at 18 minutes by the maximum heart rate rather than determining the difference in the heart rates as a percentage of the maximum heart rate. The percentage change was a decrease, so the answer had to show this in words or by use of the negative sign. Candidates should be encouraged to write out their working as it is possible in multi-step calculations to give partial credit if they make an error in their calculation.
notes.3diii: Only a few candidates answered this question in sufficient detail. Candidates often stated that there was more blood flow, but they did not state that this occurs to the muscles. A common error was to state that blood flow increases to the body. Candidates recognised that there was a need for more oxygen, but often omitted to state that it was for respiration or that more energy was needed for contraction of the muscles. Some mentioned carbon dioxide and lactic acid, but rarely explained that the increased blood flow would help remove these waste products of respiration from the muscles.
notes.4ai: Some candidates answered this well, but others confused urea with urine. Others missed that it is excess amino acids that are deaminated.
notes.4aii: A few candidates correctly identified that urea is transported in the blood plasma.
notes.4aiii: Most candidates correctly stated that urea is toxic. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
notes.4aiv: Many candidates named the renal vein as the blood vessel that carries blood away from the kidney. Incorrect answers included the renal artery, the hepatic vein, and the hepatic portal vein.
notes.4b: Many candidates were confused about the process of urine formation. Very few candidates described it in sufficient detail. There was confusion over the role of filtration and reabsorption. There were errors stating where reabsorption takes place. Few explained that all the glucose that is filtered from the blood plasma is reabsorbed and few stated that urine consists of urea, excess water, and excess ions.
notes.4c: Some candidates gave enough detail to gain marks for explaining the importance of nitrate ions to plants. Most simply stated that nitrate ions are required for growth, energy or to prevent yellow leaves and did not gain credit. Others stated that nitrate ions are used to make amino acids that in turn are used to make proteins, but then did not state that these are required for growth.
notes.4d: Some good suggestions of precautions that the farmer should take to reduce the risk of eutrophication occurring in the lake were seen. Common answers were using a minimal mass of fertiliser and spraying only during dry weather, thereby reducing the chance of run-off.
notes.5a: Most candidates described the role of progesterone in maintaining the lining of the uterus during pregnancy. Some also stated that progesterone prevents the release of FSH and LH.
notes.5bi: Many candidates gave two useful substances that move from mother to fetus. The term nutrients was not accepted.
notes.5bii: Many good answers were seen for this question showing a good understanding of the adaptations for efficient diffusion across the placenta. A minority of candidates discussed air spaces and ventilation which are incorrect in this context.
notes.5c: Most candidates completed the Punnett square although some used incorrect genotypes for the gametes. The error carried forward principle was applied when this happened. Candidates should use the letters for the alleles given in the stem of the question. The alleles given were D and d . Some candidates used R and h instead, which suggests two different genes are involved in controlling the Rhesus blood group system. Some also used the notation for sex-linked genes including the X and Y chromosomes.
notes.6ai: Some candidates read the figures correctly from the graph, but many did not identify a 10-year period. The correct answer was the 1950s.
notes.6aii: Many good answers were seen here with most candidates giving a detailed description of how humans have caused deforestation.
notes.6bi: Many candidates calculated the mass of protein in one seed correctly. Answers that were rounded to two or three decimal places were accepted.
notes.6bii: Many candidates described the purpose of seed banks, rather than why plants can be conserved using seed banks. Good answers included the suggestions that many seeds are dormant and that most require little space for storage.
notes.6biii: Most candidates gave the importance of conservation projects in preventing extinction, maintaining biodiversity, and protecting ecosystems, but very few gave any further description. Those who expanded their answers included ideas of providing the sources of new drugs, genes, and crop plants, and for future research.
notes.7a: Most candidates correctly stated that nitrogen was found in all proteins but not in carbohydrates. Some stated sulfur but this is not found in all proteins. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
notes.7b: Most candidates correctly completed the rows for glycogen and protein in Table 7.1, but few could provide correct answers for the rows on starch and oil.
notes.7c: Many correct answers were seen, although some candidates appeared not to understand the term hormone and gave substances other than insulin, glucagon, and adrenaline. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
